findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, risking cross-identity collisions
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from namespace, userUID, action, name and parent only. Subjects of different identity types can share the same UID string (e.g. `user:0`, `anonymous:0`, `render:0`, or a service account whose UID equals a user UID), so a denial recorded for one identity can be returned as a cached deny for a different identity in Check (service.go:116-121). Unlike permCache, which uses distinct key builders per identity type (anonymousPermCacheKey vs userPermCacheKey), the denial key has no type discriminator. This produces incorrect authz decisions (wrongful denials, and incorrect caching semantics). Include the identity type in the key.

findings.title: Cached denials are not invalidated when permissions are granted
findings.body: Check now stores a positive deny entry (permDenialCache, shortCacheTTL=30s) for every (namespace, user, action, name, parent) that is denied after a DB query, and returns early on a hit without consulting the DB. There is no invalidation path when a permission is subsequently granted (e.g. a user is given access to an existing dashboard/folder immediately after being denied), so the user will keep receiving 403s for up to 30 seconds even though the fresh DB state allows access. This is the inverse of the problem the PR fixes; consider a shorter TTL or an invalidation hook.

findings.title: Per-resource denial cache entries can grow unboundedly
findings.body: The denial cache key includes the resource name and parent folder, so every distinct denied resource for every user creates a separate entry in the shared local cache. In workloads where many checks are denied (e.g. scanning/listing a large number of dashboards per user), this produces a very large number of cache entries with no bound other than the 30s TTL and 2–10 min cleanup interval, increasing memory pressure on the shared cache that also holds permissions, teams and folder trees.

findings.title: permissionCacheUsage metric double-counted / wrongly labelled in Check
findings.body: In Check, a denial-cache hit increments permissionCacheUsage with label "true" and returns; on a permission-cache hit that results in allow it also increments "true"; but on a permission-cache hit that results in deny the code falls through and increments "false" at line 137 even though the cache was hit. The metric therefore no longer reflects cache hit ratio and mixes denial-cache hits with permission-cache hits, making it unusable for tuning.

findings.title: Non-ErrNotFound errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are silently ignored
findings.body: getCachedIdentityPermissions can return real errors (e.g. GetUserIdentifiers store failure, or 'unsupported identity type'). In Check (line 123) and List (line 180) any error is treated the same as a cache miss, so genuine backend failures are swallowed and the code proceeds to a second lookup; the error cause is lost from logs/traces. Distinguish cache.ErrNotFound from other errors.

findings.title: cacheHit test field is now dead and cached-permission path untested in getUserPermissions
findings.body: The 'should return permissions from cache if available' case was removed from TestService_getUserPermissions, leaving the cacheHit field always false and the `if tc.cacheHit` branches (lines 367-369, 388-392) unreachable. Since getUserPermissions no longer reads permCache, there is no test asserting that it always re-queries the store (the behaviour change this PR relies on), nor that the permission cache is still written. Add an explicit assertion that the store is queried even when permCache is populated.
